==English== ===Alternative forms=== * {{alt|en|lak||pronunciation spelling|AAVE}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|līk}}, {{IPA|en|/laɪ̯k/}} * {{IPA|en|/læ̙ːk/|/lɑːk/|a=MLE,Jamaica}} * {{IPA|en|/lɔɪ̯k/|a=Dublin}} * {{IPA|en|/lʌɪk/|[ləi̯k]|a=CA,Scotland}} * {{IPA|en|/lɑɪ̯k/|a=Australia}} * {{audio|en|en-uk-to like.ogg|a=UK|text=to like}} * {{audio|en|en-us-like.ogg|a=US}} * {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-like.wav|a=Southern England}} * {{rhymes|en|aɪk|s=1}} ===Etymology 1=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*leyg-|id=like}} Verb from {{inh|en|enm|liken}}, from {{inh|en|ang|līcian||to like, to please}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*līkēn}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*līkāną}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*leyg-||image; likeness; similarity}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|liekje||to be similar, resemble}}, {{cog|fy|lykje||to seem, appear, look}}, {{cog|nl|lijken||to seem}}, {{cog|nds|lieken||to be like; resemble}}, {{cog|de|gleichen||to resemble}}, {{cog|sv|lika||to like; put up with; align with}}, {{cog|no|like||to like}}, {{cog|is|-}} and {{cog|fo|líka||to like}}. Noun from {{inh|en|enm|like|t=pleasure, will, like}}, from the verb {{der|en|enm|liken|t=to like}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{sid|en|enjoy}} To [[enjoy]], be pleased by; [[favor]]; be in favor of. #: {{ant|en|dislike|hate|mislike|disapprove}} #: {{ux|en|I '''like''' reading [[books]].}} #: {{ux|en|I [[very much]] '''like''' hamburgers.}} #: {{ux|en|I '''like''' skiing in winter very much.}} #: {{ux|en|I '''liked''' her much better after I [[got to know]] her.}} #: {{ux|en|I '''like''' it when you sing.}} #* {{RQ:Locke Human Understanding|2|21|text=He may either go or stay, as he best '''likes'''.}} #* {{RQ:Chambers Younger Set|VIII|passage=At her invitation he outlined for her the succeeding chapters with terse military accuracy ; and what she '''liked''' best and best understood was avoidance of that false modesty which condescends, turning technicality into pabulum.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive|archaic}} To [[please]] {{q|same meaning as above but with subject and object reversed}}. ##* {{quote-book|en|author=Sir {{w|Philip Sidney}}| passage=I willingly confess that it '''likes''' me much better when I find virtue in a fair lodging than when I am bound to seek it in an ill-favoured creature.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7ZpMAAAAcAAJ&pg=RA1-PA83&dq=dunghill.&hl=en&sa=X&ved=0ahUKEwinxIyUndDiAhWwmeAKHXD6BmQQ6AEINTAC#v=onepage&q=dunghill.&f=false| title=The Countess of Pembroke's Arcadia|year=16th century}} ## {{lb|en|obsolete}} To derive [[pleasure]] {{+obj|en|:of/:by/:with}}. ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1662|author={{w|Sir_Thomas_Salusbury,_2nd_Baronet|Thomas Salusbury}}|title=Galileo's Dialogue Concerning the Two Systems of the World|section=(Dialogue Two)|passage=And therefore it is the best way, if you '''like of''' it, to examine these taken from experiments touching the Earth, and then proceed to those of the other kind.}} ##* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=I|page=2|passage=He used to drop into my chambers once in a while to smoke, and was first-rate company. When I gave a dinner there was generally a cover laid for him. I '''liked''' the man for his own sake, and even had he promised to turn out a celebrity it would have had no weight with me.}} # To prefer and [[maintain]] (an action) as a regular [[habit]] or [[activity]]. #: {{ux|en|I '''like''' to go to the dentist every six months.}} #: {{ux|en|She '''likes''' to keep herself physically fit.}} #: {{ux|en|We '''like''' to keep one around the office just in case.}} #* {{quote-av|1=en|year=2016|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171014193917/https://learningenglish.voanews.com/a/lets-learn-english-lesson-6-where-is-the-gym/3225958.html|title=VOA Learning English (public domain)|passage=People in Washington '''like''' to work out!}} # To [[find]] [[attractive]]; to prefer the company of; to have mild romantic feelings for. #: {{syn|en|fancy|q1=British|enjoy|love}} #: {{ant|en|dislike|hate|mislike}} #: {{ux|en|I really '''like''' Sandra but don't know how to tell her.}} #* {{quote-video game|en|date=2016-12-19|location=Japan|publisher=NTT Solmare|title=Moe! Ninja Girls|system=iOS, Android|scene=Season 1, Enju Ending|text= ―{{nbsp}}Enju: “Apparently when you '''like''' someone, you start talking like them.”}} #* {{RQ:Time|title=The Danger of Surrendering Your Financial Independence in a Relationship|date=April 22 2026|author=Jillian Sanders |text=I was dating someone I '''liked''', but not enough to marry. |url=https://time.com/article/2026/04/17/the-danger-of-surrendering-your-financial-independence-in-a-relationship/ |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260422181713/https://time.com/article/2026/04/17/the-danger-of-surrendering-your-financial-independence-in-a-relationship/}} # {{lb|en|with 'would' and in certain other phrases}} To [[want]], [[desire]]. ''See also '''''[[would like]]'''''.'' #: {{ux|en|Would you '''like''' a cigarette?}} #: {{ux|en|We could go to the museum if you '''like'''.}} #: {{ux|en|May I leave now? ~ If you '''like'''.}} #: {{ux|en|I don't '''like''' to disturb him when he's working.}} #: {{ux|en|You can [[come over]] whenever you '''like'''.}} # {{senseid|en|show approval of via an online vote}} {{lb|en|Internet|social media|transitive}} To show [[support]] for, or [[approval]] of, something posted on the [[Internet]] by marking it with a [[vote]]. #: {{ant|en|unlike#Verb|dislike#Verb}} #: {{cot|en|heart|love}} #: {{ux|en|I '''liked''' my friend's last status on Facebook.}} #: {{ux|en|I can't stand Bloggs' tomato ketchup, but I '''liked''' it on Facebook so I could enter a competition.}} # {{n-g|Of inanimate objects:}} ## {{lb|en|informal|personification}} To be prone to. ##: {{usex|en|Too bad this cheese '''likes''' to stick to the pan and ruin the whole meal.}} ## {{lb|en|informal|usually in the negative}} Of a computer or other system: to tolerate as an input; to accept. ##: {{ux|en|This self-service checkout doesn't seem to '''like''' my credit card.}} ##: {{ux|en|We were frustrated that our seeming innocent choice for a team name was rejected by the game. Apparently somewhere in the name is a word that the algorithm doesn’t '''like'''.}} ##: {{usex|en|email delivery failed: remote host does not '''like''' recipient}} # {{lb|en|archaic}} To come near; to avoid with difficulty; to escape narrowly. #: {{ux|en|He '''liked''' to have been too late.}} #* {{quote-book|en|title=The Letters of Horace Walpole: Fourth Earl of Oxford|author=w:Horace Walpole|section=to George Montagu|year=1760|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8xYQAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA440&dq=troops+expedition+Kensington+Garden.&hl=en&sa=X&ved=0ahUKEwikp4TOn9DiAhXSmeAKHWOyBvQQ6AEINDAC&q=troops%20expedition%20Kensington%20Garden.&f=false|passage=He probably got his death, as he '''liked''' to have done two years ago, by viewing the troops for the expedition from the wall of Kensington Garden.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} To have an appearance or expression; to look; to seem to be (in a specified condition). #* {{RQ:Shakespeare As You Like It|act=II|scene=iv|passage=You '''like''' well, and bear your years very well.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} To [[liken]]; to [[compare]]. =====Usage notes===== * In its senses of “enjoy” and “maintain as a regular habit”, {{m|en||like}} is a [[catenative verb]]; in the former, it usually takes a [[gerund]] ({{m|en|-ing}} form), while in the latter, it takes a {{m|en|to}}-[[infinitive]]. ''See also'' [[Appendix:English catenative verbs]]. * ''Like'' is only used to mean “want” in certain expressions, such as ''[[if you like]]'' and ''[[would like]]''. The conditional form, {{m|en|would like}}, is used quite freely as a polite synonym for {{m|en|want}}. =====Conjugation===== {{en-conj|stem=lik|old=1}} =====Derived terms===== {{col3|en Conjunction from {{inh|en|enm|like}}, {{m|enm|lyke}}, {{m|enm|lik}}, {{m|enm|lyk}}, from the adverb {{der|en|enm|like}}. If they do not now accept our terms, they may expect a rain of ruin from the air, the '''like''' of which has never been seen on this Earth.}} #* {{RQ:Adams Life|page=93|text=In fact it would be fair to say that he had reached a level of annoyance the '''like''' of which had never been seen in the Universe.}} # {{lb|en|golf}} The [[stroke]] that [[equalize]]s the number of strokes played by the opposing player or side. #: {{ux|en|to play the '''like'''}} =====Synonyms===== * {{l|en|ilk}} =====Antonyms===== * {{l|en|antithesis}}, {{l|en|opposite}} =====Derived terms===== * {{l|en|and the like}} * {{l|en|like-for-like}} * {{l|en|likeless}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|something similar to a given person or object}} * Arabic: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * German: * Greek: * Hungarian: * Irish: * Portuguese: * Scottish Gaelic: * Spanish: * Swedish: {{trans-bottom}} ====Conjunction==== {{en-head|conj}} # {{lb|en|colloquial}} [[as|As]], [[the way]]. #* '''1966''', Advertising slogan for {{w|Winston cigarettes}} #*: {{w|Winston tastes good like a cigarette should|Winston tastes good '''like''' a cigarette should}} #* {{quote-song|en|year=1978|title=Do Unto Others|author=w:Bob Dylan |passage=But if you do right to me, baby

'''Like''' you’d have them, '''like''' you’d have them, do unto you}} # {{lb|en|usually|colloquial}} [[as if|As if]]; [[as though]]. #: {{ux|en|It [[look like|looks '''like''']] you've finished the project.}} #: {{ux|en|It seemed '''like''' you didn't care.}} #: {{ux|en|He didn’t have many friends, it didn’t seem '''like'''.}} # {{lb|en|usually|colloquial}} [[such as|Such as]]. #: {{ux|en|Why don’t we do something useful '''like''' clean the kitchen?}} =====Usage notes===== * ''{{w|The American Heritage Dictionary}}'' opines that using ''like'' as a conjunction, instead of ''as'', ''the way'', ''as if'', or ''as though'', is strictly [[Appendix:Glossary#informal|informal]]; it has, however, been routine since the [[Middle English]] period. ''AHD4'' says, "Writers since Chaucer's time have used ''like'' as a conjunction, but 19th-century and 20th-century critics have been so vehement in their condemnations of this usage that a writer who uses the construction in formal style risks being accused of illiteracy or worse", and recommends using ''as'' in formal speech and writing. ''{{w|The Oxford English Dictionary}}'' does not tag it as colloquial or [[Appendix:Glossary#nonstandard|nonstandard]], but notes, "Used as conj[unction]: = 'like as', 'as'. Now generally condemned as vulgar or slovenly, though examples may be found in many recent writers of standing." =====Derived terms===== See [[:Category:English similes]]. {{col3|en |be like |feel like |make like|like a plasterer's radio |like there were no tomorrow |look like |seem like |sound like }} ====Preposition==== {{en-head|prep}} # Similar to, [[reminiscent]] of. #: {{ux|en|Folk '''like''' that I just can’t brook.}} #: {{ux|en|I’m very '''like''' my father.}} #* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=2|passage=Sunning himself on the board steps, I saw for the first time Mr. Farquhar Fenelon Cooke. How high school!}} =====Usage notes===== The use as a quotative is informal; it is commonly used by young people, and commonly disliked by older generations, especially in repeated use. It may be combined with the use of the present tense as a narrative. (For its use preceded by a form of ''be'', see ''[[be like]]''.) Similar terms are ''to go'' and ''all'', as in ''I go, “Why did you do that?” and he goes, “I don't know”'' and ''I was all, “Why did you do that?” and he was all, “I don't know.”'' These expressions can imply that the attributed remark which follows is representative rather than necessarily an exact quotation; however, in speech these structures do tend to require mimicking the original speaker's inflection in a way {{m|en|said}} would not. =====Synonyms===== * {{sense|delayed filler}} [[I mean]], [[you know]] * {{sense|mild intensifier}} [[I mean]], [[well]], [[you know]] * {{sense|indicating
